name: postings-qa
tagline: A job-postings pipeline with a data-QA core: every rejected row says why.
summary: Pulls listings from public job APIs (Remotive, Greenhouse, Lever, USAJOBS, Adzuna), normalises salaries, dates and HTML before validating, runs nine rule-based quality checks that reject bad rows with a stated reason, keeps a deduplicated SQLite history with first-seen and last-seen timestamps, and turns the result into an Excel workbook with native charts and a Streamlit dashboard. A QA preview re-runs the checks over stored history with the filters you are about to save and shows exactly which listings would flip. Scrapers exist but ship off; the defaults are APIs with attribution.

data.angle: Nine auditable checks reject a listing with the check name and reason attached; stable ids per source and first-seen / last-seen timestamps make dedup across runs a fact, not a guess.

swe.angle: Adapters split fetch from pure parse so 44 tests run offline on saved responses; the UI starts runs as subprocesses, so a failing adapter cannot take the dashboard down.

highlights: Every rejected listing carries the names of the checks it failed and the reason text, so a filter decision can be inspected rather than trusted.
Normalisation happens before validation: free-text salaries become min, max, currency and period and are annualised; relative dates and epoch milliseconds become dates.
The QA preview re-runs the checks over stored history with the filters you are about to save and shows which listings would flip, before anything is written.
Parsers take decoded payloads, not URLs, so every adapter is tested against a saved API response and no test touches the network.
Runs started from the UI are child processes whose logs are tailed; Stop kills the whole process group, and the settings forms write config.yaml through a round-trip loader that keeps its comments.
